name: eBay used bare H100 SXM5 80GB module (single-module listing, tested)
price_basis: USED / Pre-Owned, BARE SXM5 module only - no HGX baseboard, no server, no NVLink fabric. $12,999.00 captured 2026-10-03, title asserts 'Tested Working'. Warranty: none from NVIDIA; seller offers 30-day returns (buyer pays return shipping) plus eBay Money Back Guarantee. Price excludes any baseboard or host.
notes: Useful because it pins down that a used H100 SXM5 MODULE is not the same product as a used 8-GPU HGX baseboard, and the gap is enormous: the same seller's ecosystem listed an 8x80GB H100 HGX GDX baseboard at $341,872.75 (~$42,734/GPU) - more than 3x the $12,999 bare-module figure. Anyone budgeting 'used H100' must state which of these they mean. A bare SXM5 module is close to unsellable without a compatible carrier. RISK: 'Tested Working' is the seller's assertion, not a burn-in report. A same-session comparable 'Nvidia H100 80GB SXM5 GPU GH100-885K-A1, before bid ask me!' listed at $14,000.00 plus delivery from a different seller, so the two public data points bracket roughly $13k-$14k for a bare used 80GB SXM5 module. Also present in the same used result set, cheaper and more usable for cheap inference: used H100 96GB SXM5 at $14,999.00, GH200 Grace Hopper dev superchip 96GB at $4,499.95 / $5,449.99, and GH100 qualification sample at $4,500.00. The GH200/qual-sample pricing is the discount channel for Hopper-class inference, and is legal where a compliant H100 sale is not - though dev kits and qual samples carry their own support limits.
